attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his Substack post. He links Politico for the news, but this description of the ban is his own.

semantics.note: The normalised wording matches the statement: the current ban is temporary and targets deployment, not research. It is a description of the order's present status, not a forecast of how long it would last.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair and ordinary. 'Temporary' means provisional legal status. 'Not research' means there was no general ban on AI research, not that research was exempt. The contract says openly that the stronger exemption reading would not hold.

evidence.note: The Garante's 30 March 2023 order is a provisional, urgent limitation on OpenAI's processing of Italians' personal data through ChatGPT, pending the inquiry. It contains no general research ban.

The regulator's own 31 March 2023 press release, labelled a news report in the packet, confirms the immediate temporary limitation on OpenAI's processing of Italian users' data. It is an official statement about the regulator's own order.

reviews.rationale: The order uses 'limitazione provvisoria', with any further decision reserved until the inquiry ends, so the measure was temporary. It is aimed at OpenAI as controller of processing through ChatGPT, which is the public service, and does not prohibit AI research in general. The order gives no research exemption for covered data, but the plain reading the contract adopts does not require one.
